reason: The defect is real. In .claude/worktrees/wf_b39793f6-e79-4/tools/overlap_probe.py (commit 9826517, wt4 clean), run_probe's try covers only registration. The overlap 'raise RuntimeError' and write_csv on the no-overlap path both run after it. Four more paths sit outside any guard: the module-writing cell, 'import overlap_reg as R' at the top of overlap_probe (executed by the run cell), kaggle_main's setup, and a dead or OOM kernel. Any of them gives 'Notebook Threw Exception', which the current G-P text reads as ERROR = overlap exists, and that would open K6. The proposed re-encoding is sound. The positive signal then needs the code to reach an explicit decision and write a deliberately malformed CSV, and every crash class becomes UNKNOWN. It changes the encoding, not a gate threshold, fits the already-approved single G-P slot, costs about 30 min of code and tests, and does not touch the finals #37 + #38. It adds one risk the finding does not mention: if the 'valid' minimal CSV were rejected by the hidden scorer, a no-overlap result would read as overlap. probe_local.json shows the dummy CSV equals sample_submission.csv line for line, so the risk is low. VALUE CAVEATS: (1) G-A FAILED as pre-registered (ga_report.json G_A_pass=false; 43/62 < 60), so by default (PC8-01) G-P is never submitted, and this fix matters only if the user logs a post-hoc 'continue'. (2) A false 'overlap' costs only one slot plus a ~7.5 h K6 run, not score: with no accepted pair, K6 is byte-identical to K2 by G-D. The gain is decision integrity, not LB. (3) The sibling 2-bit probe (scan_hypotheses r8h) contains this crash separation; implement one encoding, not both.
fix: Apply only if the user continues after the G-A FAIL (PC8-01), and log the change in CONTEXT with date -u before the submit. (a) Run cell: wrap the whole body, including 'import overlap_probe' / 'import overlap_reg' and kaggle_main(), in an outer try/except BaseException-minus-KeyboardInterrupt. On an unexpected error, delete any submission.csv and write none ('CSV Not Found'). (b) decide(): 'raise' becomes 'malformed'. After a successful registration with >= 1 accepted pair, write submission.csv as the LAST action with a wrong header (e.g. a single column 'overlap_probe' and 1 row), so the hidden run gives 'Submission Scoring / Format Error'. No pair: the valid minimal CSV, unchanged and still == sample_submission format (keep test_csv_equals_sample_submission_on_dummy; if the local metric is available, also score one hidden-shaped minimal CSV without error). The commit run on 4 clips always writes the valid CSV. (c) Class table in CONTEXT BEFORE the submit: COMPLETE -> no overlap -> stop the line; 'Scoring/Format Error' -> overlap (only if the commit run COMPLETED); 'CSV Not Found', 'Threw Exception', 'Notebook Timeout', 'Exceeded Compute', 'Kaggle Error' -> UNKNOWN -> no K6, ask the user. (d) Read the class with the C2 API command (error_description), falling back to the Submissions page. (e) Unit tests: every branch, including an exception injected in the import and write steps -> no CSV, and overlap -> malformed CSV that the local format check rejects. (f) If the team adopts the 2-bit probe instead, carry (a)-(e) into it.
realistic_gain: No LB gain on public or private. It prevents a false 'overlap exists' read, which would cost one wasted K6 slot and a ~7.5 h run (score harm ~0, since K6 == K2 with no accepted pair) and would mislead the K6/finals decision log. Zero value if the user keeps the default STOP after the G-A FAIL (43/62).
